title: API 570 Training in Tulsa, OK: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: Online, self-paced API 570 exam prep for Tulsa piping inspectors: refinery interconnects, coker and lube lines, CUI and CML programmes, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 570 Training in Tulsa: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Refinery, Midstream and Contract UT Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors in Tulsa

A refinery holds far more pipe than vessels, and most API 570 candidates spend their working days walking circuits, marking condition monitoring locations and reviewing thickness data rather than climbing inside drums. In Tulsa that work centres on HF Sinclair's refinery and on the contract inspection and NDT companies that serve it and the other Oklahoma plants. Tulsa is also where ONEOK has its headquarters, and in September 2023 ONEOK completed its purchase of Magellan Midstream Partners, another Tulsa-based company, so pipeline work is part of the local picture and some candidates come to API 570 from it. This page is written for both groups.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Tulsa. You prepare online, setting your own pace, with an instructor who answers questions as they come up, which suits people who work rotations or turnarounds. API sets the eligibility requirements, administers the API 570 examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. Atlantis is not approved by API as a training provider, and completing the course is not the same as being certified.

Two plants two miles apart, joined by pipe

When Holly bought Sunoco's Tulsa refinery and then Sinclair's in 2009, it set out to run them as one. Its annual report for that year described interconnect pipelines that would carry intermediate streams between the facilities, with high sulfur diesel and gas oil streams going from the west plant and heavy oil streams from the east. HF Sinclair now describes a single Tulsa refinery of 125,000 barrels per day, while EIA's survey of capacity at the start of 2026 still lists Tulsa East and Tulsa West as separate plants.

For a piping inspector, integration of that kind changes the picture in three ways:

  • Longer circuits. Streams that once stayed inside one plant now travel between two, so the circuits carrying them cover more ground and more records.
  • New dead legs. Lines that were active before the integration can end up on standby or stagnant, which is how dead legs are created.
  • Changed corrosivity. A stream's behaviour can change when its destination or temperature changes, so a rate measured before the change can mislead.

How the interconnecting lines are classified and inspected is the owner's decision. For the examination, what matters is knowing what API 570's scope includes and excludes, and how an owner assigns piping classes. Atlantis's note on the boundary between API 570 and pipeline codes sets out the usual dividing lines.

Piping the coker, lube and asphalt units add

EIA lists vacuum distillation, a delayed coker of 9,300 barrels per stream day, and lubricant and asphalt production capacity at Tulsa West, and HF Sinclair says the site produces base oils, process oils, horticultural oils, asphalt modifiers and wax. Heavy products of that kind are moved hot or kept warm, so steam tracing, heated lines and insulation are everywhere on that side of the refinery. Hot hydrocarbon lines raise sulfidation, and coker and slurry lines raise erosion, two of the mechanisms the API 570 Body of Knowledge lists.

On the east side, the catalytic reformer belongs to a type of unit that RP 571 names in its discussion of hydrochloric acid corrosion, and the cat cracker's gas plant and the light-ends handling on both sites put propane and butane in the pipe racks. When an exam question describes a line in light hydrocarbon service, check it against the class definitions in API 570 before you choose an interval; the guide to piping service classes shows how the classes are decided.

Corrosion under insulation through an Oklahoma year

Corrosion under insulation reaches the API 570 exam through RP 571 and RP 574, and it is a mechanism a Tulsa piping inspector manages all year. Oklahoma's hot, humid summers, heavy spring storms and winter freezes give water every chance to get under jacketing. It enters at damaged or badly lapped cladding, at unsealed penetrations, around pipe supports and at the low points of vertical runs, and leaking steam tracers on the heated lube and asphalt lines add water from the inside.

RP 571 explains the operating temperatures at which carbon steel and austenitic stainless steel are most susceptible, and it warns about equipment that cycles through those temperatures or runs intermittently. Learn the ranges from the code text rather than from a summary, because exam distractors are often built from figures that are nearly right. In practice the inspection starts with a visual survey of the insulation system, followed by targeted examination where the jacketing is damaged or the line operates in the susceptible range; API 570 expects the extent of that work to rise with the consequence of a leak. The CUI detection guide compares the methods.

CMLs, injection points and dead legs on an integrated site

Condition monitoring locations are only useful if the same spot is read the same way each time. On a site that combined two refineries' records, the first job is often to check that CML numbering, reading positions and nominal thicknesses agree from one survey to the next, because a reading taken a few inches from the last one can invent a corrosion rate. Grid elbows and tees where flow changes direction, place more CMLs where corrosion is localised, and keep the general-loss circuits sparse.

Injection points, where wash water, neutraliser, inhibitor or another chemical enters a process stream, are treated by API 570 as circuits of their own, with their own inspection expectations and more frequent attention than the line around them. The injection point guide explains how the circuit is laid out. Dead legs need the opposite thinking: the risk sits where nothing moves, at the low point and at the junction with the live line, and in an Oklahoma winter a stagnant branch can also freeze and split. Small-bore connections and soil-to-air interfaces complete the list of places where a CML programme usually under-samples.

Worked example: sizing a replacement spool, mill tolerance included

Repairs and replacements bring a calculation the exam asks in several forms: what wall must new pipe have? Suppose a 6-inch carbon steel spool, outside diameter 6.625 in., is to be replaced in a line designed for 450 psig. Assume for this illustration a B31.3 allowable stress of 20,000 psi at the design temperature, seamless pipe with E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4 and an owner's corrosion allowance of 0.0625 in.

  1. Pressure design thickness from B31.3 304.1.2: t = PD ÷ 2(SEW + PY) = (450 × 6.625) ÷ 2(20,000 + 180) = 2,981.25 ÷ 40,360 = 0.074 in.
  2. Check the formula applies. B31.3 uses it where t is less than D/6, here 1.10 in., so it does.
  3. Add the allowances under 304.1.1: tm = t + c = 0.074 + 0.0625 = 0.136 in.
  4. Allow for the mill's minus tolerance. Seamless pipe made with a 12.5% under-tolerance must have a nominal wall of at least 0.136 ÷ 0.875 = 0.156 in.

Two traps hide in questions like this. The first is forgetting the mill tolerance and choosing a wall that meets 0.136 in. only on paper. The second appears later in service: API 570 judges the installed pipe against the greater of the pressure design thickness and the owner's structural minimum, so a 6-inch line whose pressure design thickness is 0.074 in. will be retired on its structural minimum if that is higher. Read each question carefully to see which of the two thicknesses it is asking about.

Getting to API 570 from a Tulsa job

For API 570, a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, or three years of technical military service, needs one year supervising or performing piping inspection. A two-year degree or certificate needs two years and a high school diploma three, counting design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of piping with at least one year in inspection; candidates without formal education need five years or more. The experience must sit within the last ten years and be gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Details are on the API 570 certification page.

  • UT thickness technicians. Readings taken for an owner's CML programme are inspection work, which makes this a common route into API 570; API judges each application on what you document. NDT training in Tulsa is where many technicians start.
  • Welders and pipefitters. Tulsa Welding School and Tulsa Tech both teach welding, and a welding background pays off in the Section IX and RP 577 questions. Construction and repair years count on the two-year and high school routes once the year of inspection is in place.
  • Pipeline staff. Integrity work on transmission pipelines regulated under federal pipeline rules is not API 570 process piping, so ask API how such experience will be treated before you apply.
  • Engineers. A degree puts you on the one-year route, and the year of inspection is what remains.

Fitting B31.3 study into a Tulsa schedule

The closed-book half rewards people who have read API 570 and RP 574 slowly and more than once, so do that reading in the months when your work is steady. Keep the open-book work for shorter sessions: practise finding Table A-1 allowable stresses, the weld joint quality factors, the leak test rules in paragraph 345 and the B16.5 rating tables quickly on a PDF, because the code files at the test centre are electronic. During a turnaround, a short daily review of definitions and the interval rules keeps the material fresh until you can return to timed practice papers. Send your questions to the instructor as they arise rather than saving them up.

Prometric lists test centres in and around Tulsa; book as soon as API confirms your eligibility. If you also inspect welding, the AWS CWI exam-prep course for Tulsa covers the separate CWI examination, and the API 570 practice questions are a quick test of where you stand.

Sponsoring piping inspectors from a Tulsa site or contractor

An employer can enrol one piping inspector or a whole UT crew, and fees are quoted on request. Because nobody has to attend a class, the people being sponsored keep working their circuits while they prepare, and each applies to API in their own name with their own experience record. The employer's part is to confirm the experience each candidate claims and to plan cover for exam days.

faq.q: Can I take API 570 training in person in Tulsa?
faq.a: There is no Atlantis classroom in Tulsa, and the API 570 course is not taught in a room anywhere: it is online and self-paced, and an instructor answers your questions as you study. You take the examination itself in person at a Prometric test centre once API has accepted your application, and API issues the certification to those who pass.

faq.q: Are the interconnect lines between Tulsa East and Tulsa West API 570 piping or pipelines?
faq.a: That is for the owner to decide and document in its procedures, based on how the lines are designed, operated and regulated. The exam does not ask about any particular site. It does expect you to know API 570's scope, the systems it excludes or makes optional, and how piping classes are assigned, so read the scope section closely and be clear about what makes a line process piping rather than a pipeline.

faq.q: Does pipeline integrity work at a Tulsa midstream company count toward API 570?
faq.a: Possibly, but do not assume so. API 570 experience is experience with piping of the kind the code covers, gained while working for or under contract to an authorized inspection agency. Transmission pipeline work regulated by federal pipeline rules is a different discipline, though skills such as UT thickness surveys and corrosion assessment carry over. Describe your duties precisely on the application and ask API before you apply if you are unsure.

faq.q: Which damage mechanisms are on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: The current Body of Knowledge limits RP 571 questions to the definitions and fifteen mechanisms: amine stress corrosion cracking, atmospheric corrosion, boiler water and steam condensate corrosion, caustic corrosion, caustic stress corrosion cracking, chloride stress corrosion cracking, corrosion under insulation, erosion, galvanic corrosion, hydrochloric acid corrosion, mechanical fatigue including vibration, microbiologically influenced corrosion, soil corrosion, acidic sour water corrosion and sulfidation. Check the effectivity sheet for your window before you study.

faq.q: Is mill tolerance tested on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: It can be, because it sits inside the B31.3 rules the exam draws on. B31.3 requires the minimum thickness of the pipe selected, allowing for the manufacturer's minus tolerance, to be at least the pressure design thickness plus allowances. Replacement and repair questions are where it usually appears. Work through the calculation in full rather than stopping at the pressure design thickness, and watch whether the question gives a nominal or a minimum wall.

faq.q: I trained as a welder in Tulsa. Can I become an API 570 inspector?
faq.a: Yes, through the experience routes. With a high school diploma API asks for three years in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of piping, including at least one year of inspection, gained within the last ten years with an authorized inspection agency. Welding and pipefitting years can count toward the total, so the step most welders still need is that year of inspection work, often as a UT or visual inspection technician.

faq.q: How do I get faster at the open-book B31.3 questions?
faq.a: Practise on a PDF, since the test centre supplies the codes electronically and you cannot bring your own marked copy. Learn the paragraph and table numbers you use most, read the notes under each table, and time yourself so that no single question takes too long. The course's timed practice papers copy the split between the closed-book and open-book halves.

faq.q: Can a Tulsa contractor enrol its UT crew for API 570 preparation?
faq.a: Yes. An inspection contractor can enrol several technicians at once, and fees are quoted on request. Each person studies at their own pace around field work, sends questions to the instructor when they need help, and applies to API individually. The contractor confirms the experience each technician claims, which API verifies as part of the application.
